`GET /invoices/<id>` now returns a 404 when the invoice doesn't exist. I couldn't run it, though: Flask isn't installed in this environment, so the check failed with `ModuleNotFoundError` before it reached the endpoint.

The change is in `src/api/invoices.py:12-13`. The handler now checks for a missing invoice before building the response. Before this, a missing invoice made it read `.__dict__` on `None`, which caused a 500 error.

The 404 uses the existing `problem()` helper from `src/api/errors.py`, so it follows the project's convention of returning errors as `application/problem+json`. The response body looks like this:

```json
{"type": "about:blank", "title": "Invoice not found", "status": 404, "detail": "No invoice with id 'abc'"}
```

To check it once Flask is installed, register the `bp` blueprint on a Flask app and request a missing ID with the test client. I didn't add a test, because the existing tests don't cover the API layer.
